title: Call for Research Proposals April 2026
text:
CALL FOR PROPOSALS FOR THE UGANDA COMMUNICATIONS
COMMISSION (UCC) RESEARCH SUPPORT TO ACADEMIA
1. INTRODUCTION
The Uganda Communications Commission (UCC) invites applications for
academic research support in line with its mandate under the Uganda
Communications Act, 2013, particularly Section 5(1)(l), which empowers the
Commission to promote research into the development and utilization of new
communications techniques and technologies.
The research support initiative also aims to enhance access to communication
services for all members of society, including persons with disabilities and other
underserved communities, in accordance with the UCC Collaboration
Framework (2022–2025).
Through this call, UCC seeks to support high-quality academic research that
advances knowledge and contributes to policy and regulatory development in
the communications sector.
2. STRATEGIC ALIGNMENT
This call is aligned with the strategic priorities of the Uganda Communications
Commission as outlined in the UCC Strategic Plan (2025/26–2029/30), whose
vision is “An Inclusive Digital Economy.” The strategic goal of the plan is to
ensure accessible, affordable, and secure digital services by 2030.
The research programme also contributes to the realization of Uganda’s broader
national development agenda, including Uganda Vision 2040, the Fourth
National Development Plan, Digital Uganda Vision, and the Uganda Digital
Transformation Roadmap.
UCC seeks to strengthen collaboration between academia, industry, and
policymakers to address emerging challenges and opportunities in the
communications sector through evidence-based research.
3. PRIORITY RESEARCH AREAS
Proposals should address one or more of the following thematic areas:
A. Sustainability and Green Transition in the Communications Sector
1

Focus on environmentally sustainable communications infrastructure and
operations.
Illustrative Research Directions (non-exhaustive):
• Incentives and frameworks for renewable energy adoption
• Barriers and opportunities for green transition
• Sustainable infrastructure development approaches
B. Next-Generation Telecommunications Infrastructure and Spectrum
Management
Focus on the deployment and management of advanced communication
technologies.
Illustrative Research Directions (non-exhaustive):
• Policy and regulatory considerations for 5G, 6G and beyond
• Adoption, use cases, and challenges of advanced technologies
• Spectrum management and backhaul evolution
C. Digital Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Emerging Technologies
Focus on ICT-driven innovation and digital transformation.
Illustrative Research Directions (non-exhaustive):
• Innovation ecosystems and entrepreneurship
• Emerging technologies (AI, IoT, data-driven systems)
• Barriers to digital enterprise development
D. Consumer Protection, Digital Rights, and Online Safety
Focus on consumer protection and safety in digital environments.
Illustrative Research Directions (non-exhaustive):
• Consumer protection challenges in digital ecosystems
• Online safety, including risks to vulnerable groups
• Approaches to harmful online content
E. Access, Affordability, and User Experience of Communication Services
Focus on inclusivity, accessibility, and service quality.
Illustrative Research Directions (non-exhaustive):
• Access and affordability of communication services
• User experience and quality of service
• Barriers affecting underserved populations
F. Consumer Awareness, Participation, and Institutional Effectiveness
Focus on consumer awareness and institutional performance.
Illustrative Research Directions (non-exhaustive):
• Consumer awareness and education initiatives
• Stakeholder participation in consumer protection
• Institutional and coordination challenges
Applicants are encouraged to define focused and well-scoped research
problems within these thematic areas.
2

4. ELIGIBLE APPLICANTS
Applications are invited from the following categories of researchers/students:
a) Undergraduate students whose projects must be supervised by a faculty
member, who will provide academic guidance throughout the research
process. Undergraduate participation is intended to strengthen research
capacity while generating context-specific insights relevant to Uganda’s
communications sector.
b) Graduate students (master’s and PhD) whose research aligns with the
highlighted UCC priority areas.
c) Post-doctoral researchers conducting advanced research in
communications-related fields, with potential to contribute to academic
and policy development.
d) Inter-university research teams, comprising academic staff and/or
students from at least two tertiary institutions.
5. RESEARCH SUPPORT CATEGORIES
The research programme will support projects under the following four funding
categories:
I. Lot 1 – Undergraduate Research Support
Support for undergraduate research aligned with UCC priority areas. This
category is designed to build foundational research capacity while encouraging
applied, context-specific studies addressing real sector challenges.
II. Lot 2 – Postgraduate Research Support
Support for Master’s and PhD research projects that demonstrate rigorous
analysis and contribute to academic knowledge and policy-relevant insights in
the communications sector.
III. Lot 3 – Inter-University Research Collaboration
Support for collaborative research involving at least two tertiary institutions,
with the lead institution based in Uganda, aimed at addressing complex and
multi-disciplinary challenges in the communications sector.
IV. Lot 4 – Academia-for-Industry Research
Support for research teams working with communications sector licensees or
operators to address industry-specific challenges through applied research and
innovation.
3

7. PROPOSAL FORMAT
Proposals must:
• Be written in Microsoft Word
• Use Times New Roman, Font Size 12
• Use single line spacing
• Not exceed 20 pages
8. REQUIRED SECTIONS
I. Title Page
II. Project Summary (Maximum 300 words)
III. Introduction and Background
IV. Problem Statement
V. Research Objectives
VI. Research Questions or Hypotheses
VII. Justification of the Study
VIII. Methodology
IX. Implementation Plan
X. Contribution to Cross-Cutting Issues (gender, disability, climate change)
XI. Literature Review (APA 7th Edition)
XII. Budget and Budget Justification
XIII. Curriculum Vitae of the research team
4

Note for Undergraduate Applicants
Undergraduate proposals should be clearly scoped and appropriate to the level of
study, with well-defined and manageable research questions.
8. SUBMISSION DETAILS
Proposals should be submitted electronically to the Link:
https://www.ucc.co.ug/call-for-research-proposals/
Submission Deadline: Monday, 8th May 2026 at 5:00 PM.
Addressed to:
Executive Director,
Uganda Communications Commission,
UCC House, Plot 42–44 Spring Road, Bugolobi
P.O. Box 7376, Kampala, Uganda.
For inquiries, send an email to Registry at registry@ucc.co.ug
9. SELECTION PROCESS
Please note that any late submissions will be rejected. The proposal should
consist of the following sections: -
a) Title Page: Include a precise research study title of not more than
20 words, name(s), Department, Faculty/School of the applicant(s),
and names of the investigator.
b) Project Summary: Maximum of 300 words.
c) Introduction and Background: Describe the need for the project, how the
proposal was developed, why the project is being proposed, how it relates to
indicator achievement, and its innovative aspects. This section should also
introduce the project and its objectives. Maximum of two pages.
d) Problem Statement: Provide a clear statement of the work to be undertaken,
including research questions and objectives. Maximum of one page.
e) Objectives/Major Research Questions: Maximum of one page
f) Research Questions/Hypotheses: Where applicable, a maximum of one
page.
g) Justification: Maximum of one page.
h) Methodology: Include a research plan specifying how the students will
spend their time on the proposed project. Elaborate on what you want to do,
how you plan to do it, your research timeline, and why you want to do it
5

(importance to your field/discipline, importance to your professional
development, etc.). Maximum of four pages. Attach separate quantitative
and/or qualitative data collection tools.
i) Implementation Plan: Maximum of one page.
j) Contribution to Cross-Cutting Issues: For example, gender, disability,
marginalised groups, and climate change, maximum of one page.
k) Literature Review: Use APA 7th edition, a maximum of two pages.
l) Budget and Budget Justification: Provide a detailed budget. If funds for
materials or equipment are requested, ensure that the costs are reasonable
and credible. Maximum of three pages.
m) Applicant’s Curriculum Vitae (Maximum one page for Principal Investigator
and one page for each Co-Principal Investigator).
10. RESTRICTIONS
The support schemes are subject to the following conditions:
1. The UCC research support to academia (undergraduate, postgraduate and
doctoral) will be limited to the following: -
a) Reimbursement of expenses (i.e., retroactive support) for completed
activity is not possible.
b) The support cannot be used for infrastructure costs normally covered by
your school or department.
c) Costs such as fees, stipends/salaries and other remuneration will not be
eligible.
d) An applicant has priority if he/she has not received prior funding from the
undergraduate research program, within the same academic year.
e) Support to more than one student delivering the same presentation
abroad.
2. The funding under the inter-university research collaborations (academic
staff and graduate/ postgraduate or post-doctorate students) shall be
restricted to the following: -
a. Reimbursement of expenses (i.e., retroactive support) for completed
activity is not possible.
b. The support cannot be used for infrastructure costs normally covered
by the Universities.
6

c. Costs such as fees, stipends/salaries and other remuneration will not
be eligible.
d. Funding shall be only for collaborating universities/ institutions of
higher learning.
A project or research proposal is required for all applicants. We encourage
students to collaborate on ideas with their research supervisors, but the proposal
must be developed and submitted by the students.
11. NOTIFICATION
The Calls for Proposals for Research Support will be uploaded on the Uganda
Communications Commission (UCC) website and will also be disseminated
by email and UCC Social Media Platforms.
12. ADMINISTRATION OF THE RESEARCH SUPPORT TO ACADEMIA
a) At the end of the selection process, the UCC will announce the successful
applicants, who will be required to sign a Bonding Agreement with the UCC.
b) The UCC will then issue the support as per the terms of the bonding
agreement.
c) Monthly progress reports shall be submitted by the recipients to the
UCC Project Implementation team.
d) A final report shall be submitted as per the approved project time frame.
13. EXPECTED OUTPUTS
On completion of the research project, recipients are expected to produce
scholarly and/or policy-relevant outputs appropriate to their level of study, with
higher-level research (Master’s, PhD, and postdoctoral) expected to demonstrate
stronger contributions to academic and policy discourse. Outputs may include:
(1) Research papers or journal publications
(2) Conference or dissemination presentations
(3) Policy-relevant insights for the communications sector
(4) Submission to the UCC Research Repository
(5) Final project report
Please note that the research project must be completed by 30th November 2026.
7

14. SELECTION AND NOTIFICATION PROCESS
Proposals will be subjected to the following process:
a) Administrative review for eligibility
b) Shortlisting of qualifying applicants
c) Evaluation and final selection by the Selection Committee
Applicants will be notified of the outcome of the shortlisting process, and
shortlisted applicants will receive further instructions.
Final results will be communicated to shortlisted applicants upon completion of
the evaluation process and will also be published on the UCC website and official
communication channels.
